Its colloidal calcium phosphate is here and dissolves as the acid arrives; casein's own buffering is not here at all, and that is about a third of milk's buffer capacity. Above pH 5 what is missing costs little; below it the colloid is spent and this beaker has nothing left to resist with, where a real one still has casein — so the number is a lower bound again, and by more than it was.
